answer: Seasoned identity tiers stop sybil floods by making age and clean history the price of volume. A new identity may run only 3 paid jobs per epoch and holds no haven for funds until it survives 14 epochs without a failed audit. Like a tundra outpost earning supply routes after a full winter, an agent climbs tiers only through verified work, so 1,000 fresh aliases buy 1,000 tiny quotas. Auditors compare timing and pricing each epoch; a cluster moving in lockstep loses its tier, forfeits payments, and restarts at zero. The fable holds: copies are cheap, but a lived record is not.
